**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed).

The MSA imposes no most-favoured-nation obligation on The Associated Press:

- **No MFN language exists.** Targeted searches for "most favoured", "most favored", "no less favorable", "best terms", and "pricing" all returned zero hits across the document's single section.
- **The commercial terms clauses are clean.** §5 (Fees and Payment, p0023) sets revenue sharing by reference to each Exhibit and addresses sequential liability, payment timing, and taxes — with no requirement that we extend Kubient terms comparable to those given to any third party, and no obligation to match third-party offers.
- **§1 actively cuts the other way** (p0001): "Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties." This preserves our freedom to deal with competing agents on whatever terms we choose — reinforcing the preferred position.

Per the rule's direction analysis, nothing binds us here, so the clause sits at the **preferred** position rather than the fallback. Worth noting in passing: the Vendor also grants us no MFN pricing, but the playbook treats a Vendor-granted MFN as welcome rather than required, so its absence is not a deviation and I have not flagged it.
